subtitle: True Peak Mastering Limiter
tagline: A stereo-linked true-peak limiter with a fixed 2 ms lookahead, program-aware release, micro-peak Enhance, and optional TPDF dither.

body.lead: TB Limiter is a stereo-linked true-peak mastering limiter built around eight decisive controls. It is not a sample clipper: CEILING is a true-peak bound, checked with fixed high-quality oversampling.

body.p: Drive density with `INPUT`, set an independent final `CEILING`, shape micro-peaks with `ENHANCE`, and control recovery with `RELEASE` and the program-aware `RMS ASSIST`. `RMS BALANCE` gently corrects persistent left-right energy drift, and `ATTACK` decides how the fixed 2 ms lookahead approaches each coming peak. Optional 16-bit or 24-bit TPDF dither completes the final delivery stage.

ul: Stereo-linked limiting with a fixed 2 ms lookahead and fixed oversampling
Release with program-aware RMS Assist: faster for isolated peaks, slower for dense material
Enhance for extra density by softening and driving short peaks
RMS Balance for slow left-right correction
Gain reduction, true-peak, and left-right balance displays
Works from 44.1 to 192 kHz with latency-aligned bypass

steps: Limiter (2 ms lookahead, ATTACK, RELEASE, RMS ASSIST)

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Limiter 1.2.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 0.4.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Limiter last on the master bus. The defaults are `INPUT` 4 dB, `CEILING` −1 dBTP, `RELEASE` 120 ms, `RMS ASSIST` 65%, and `ATTACK` 2 ms.
Set `CEILING` {{5}} to the true-peak limit of your delivery. −1 dBTP is a common choice for streaming.
Raise `INPUT` until the music is as loud and dense as you want, watching LIMIT GR {{2}}.
Adjust `RELEASE` and `ATTACK` {{7}}, and balance recovery with `RMS ASSIST` {{8}}.
Add `ENHANCE` {{6}} only if you need more density.
Turn on `DITHER` {{9}} only for the final 16-bit or 24-bit export, and only if your DAW does not dither.

rows: Sets how hard the signal drives the limiter. More input means more gain reduction and density; the ceiling stays the same, so compare at matched loudness.
Sets the maximum true-peak output level.
Adds density by softening and driving short peaks before the limiter. The upper half is intentionally aggressive and can change colour.
Sets how quickly gain moves toward a predicted peak within the fixed 2 ms lookahead. It does not change the latency.
Sets how quickly limiting recovers. Very short values can pump.
Adapts recovery: faster for isolated peaks and slower for dense material. It blends with RELEASE rather than replacing it.
Gently corrects persistent left-right level imbalance. It reacts slowly and does not correct short stereo movement.
Adds final TPDF dither for 16-bit or 24-bit delivery. Leave it off when the DAW will dither.

body.p: TB Limiter has a fixed latency: the 2 ms lookahead plus the oversampling filters. The plug-in reports it to the host and keeps bypass latency-aligned, so the track stays in time. TB Limiter has no compressor stage, no multiband or spectral processing, no separate clipper, and no automatic loudness target.

warn.text: Dither only adds TPDF noise; the host or exporter still converts to the final word length. Use it only on the very last export, after all gain changes and sample-rate conversion, and never on float files, stems, or when the DAW already dithers.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows, or open the list to choose a factory or user preset. Save stores the current settings as a user preset. Undo and Redo step through recent parameter changes. All factory presets use a −1 dBTP ceiling and a 2 ms attack, with dither off.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.
